smallTalk: The harvest was good this year, thanks be to the gods.
The roads are safe, as long as you travel by day.
The bells rang all week for the feast.
Every week a new pamphlet, every month a new war.
The post rides faster than ever.
The smoke never lifts over the mills.
The news never stops, day or night.
Everything is on the radio now.
The maglev was late again. Some things never change.
Everyone at home says the timeline feels different lately.

places.moment: Thebes during the reign of Hatshepsut, c. 1470 BCE (her architect Senenmut; 'scribes of the fields' re-measuring land with knotted ropes after each Nile flood)
smallTalk: The Nile rose right on time; the fields are black and rich.

places.moment: Mamluk Cairo under al-Nasir Muhammad, c. 1340 CE (the al-Khalij al-Nasiri canal was dug in 1325 and the Nile flood was read at the Roda Nilometer)
Ottoman Cairo, c. 1700 (Cairo as hub of the Red Sea coffee trade; the yearly cutting of the Khalij canal dam at the Nile flood)
Cairo in 1869, the year Khedive Isma'il opened the Suez Canal, during the building of the new irrigation canal network
Egypt under Gamal Abdel Nasser, Cairo and Aswan, c. 1962 (Aswan High Dam under construction 1960-70; Suez Canal nationalised 1956)
Babylon under Hammurabi, c. 1760 BCE (the law code, clay contracts sealed with cylinder seals)
smallTalk: The scribes are busy; every jar of barley gets its tablet.

places.moment: Baghdad under the Abbasids, c. 830 CE (al-Khwarizmi at the House of Wisdom; translation and algebra)
Baghdad under the governor Hasan Pasha (1704-1723), whose household grew into the Mamluk regime, c. 1720 (notaries recording contracts for the qadi court registers)
Baghdad under the reforming governor Midhat Pasha, c. 1870 (Iraq's first printing press and first newspaper, al-Zawra, 1869)
Baghdad c. 1956, the Development Board's modernist building boom (commissions for Gropius, Le Corbusier and Wright) in the city where Zaha Hadid grew up
Athens in the age of Pericles and Socrates, c. 430 BCE
smallTalk: Everyone argues in the agora, and nobody agrees.

places.moment: Mystras, capital of the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea, in the circle of the philosopher Gemistos Plethon, c. 1430
Greek Orthodox merchant community of Ioannina (Epirus) under Ottoman rule, c. 1700
Athens, new capital of the independent Greek kingdom, c. 1860
Athens after the fall of the junta and the restoration of democracy, c. 1975
Rome in the last years of the Republic, under Julius Caesar, c. 50 BCE
smallTalk: The Senate talks, the legions march.

places.moment: Florence of the Medici bank, during the Council of Florence, 1439
Milan under Ludovico Sforza, while Leonardo da Vinci painted the Last Supper and designed machines, c. 1495
Bologna and Pontecchio, where young Guglielmo Marconi ran his first radio experiments, 1895
Rome during the economic miracle, the year of 'La Dolce Vita', 1960
Luoyang, the Eastern Han capital, c. 105 CE, when Cai Lun presented his improved paper to the court
Kaifeng, the Northern Song capital, c. 1075. This is the era of Shen Kuo, scholar-official and envoy to the Liao, and of the magnetic compass and movable type.
Suzhou and Jiangnan in the late Ming, c. 1635, during the printing and publishing boom that produced Song Yingxing's illustrated technology encyclopedia Tiangong Kaiwu (1637)
Shanghai in the late Qing, c. 1880: the Shenbao newspaper, the Jiangnan Arsenal translation bureau and the first telegraph lines
Beijing, c. 1972, when Tu Youyou's Project 523 team isolated artemisinin at the Academy of Traditional Chinese Medicine
Yamato (the Nara–Osaka plain) in the Kofun period, c. 450 CE, the age of the great keyhole tombs and haniwa clay figures
Kyoto under the Ashikaga shogunate, c. 1400: Kitayama culture, Noh theatre, and Japanese folding fans exported to Ming China
Edo and Sunpu at the founding of the Tokugawa shogunate, c. 1610, in Tokugawa Ieyasu's time. He received a Spanish mechanical clock in 1611.
Nagoya in the Meiji period, c. 1899, the time of Sakichi Toyoda's steam-powered wooden loom (1896) and Japan's rapid industrialisation
Tokyo during the Walkman boom, c. 1980, as Akio Morita's Sony took Japanese electronics global
Camulodunum (Colchester), the trading capital of the Catuvellauni under Cunobelinus, c. 20 CE: shortly before the Roman conquest, while wine and luxury goods were arriving from Roman Gaul
London under Edward the Confessor, c. 1050: a North Sea port trading wool and silver, where laws of the time mention merchants from Flanders, Normandy and the German Empire
The Royal Exchange in London, c. 1600, the year the East India Company received its charter
London in 1843, when Ada Lovelace published her notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine, as the Cooke-Wheatstone electric telegraph spread and just before Railway Mania (1845-47)
Manchester, c. 1950, where Alan Turing was working on the university's pioneering stored-program computer (the Manchester Mark 1, built commercially by Ferranti)
Free Germania east of the Rhine and north of the Danube, c. 98 CE, as described in Tacitus' Germania
The Rhine cities of Strasbourg and Mainz, c. 1440, when Johannes Gutenberg was running his first experiments with movable metal type

Nuremberg c. 1525: Duerer's city and Europe's hub of printing and precision instruments (Henlein's early portable spring-driven clocks, Behaim's globe), the year the city council adopted the Reformation as Luther's printed pamphlets spread
Berlin c. 1899, during the boom in German electrical engineering (Siemens, AEG) and chemistry (Bayer's aspirin, synthetic dyes), when Berlin's permanent dress-reform exhibition opened
Berlin c. 1926, the Weimar Republic's golden age of science and design: Einstein directs the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics, and the Bauhaus has just moved to Dessau
Solar arcologies along the Nile, 2150, the year the office keeps
Baghdad replanted as a garden city of vertical farms, 2150
An island commonwealth running on wave power, 2150
Rome as the seat of a Mediterranean Union, 2150
Shanghai as a megacity capital linked by maglev, 2150
Neo-Tokyo built out over the bay, 2150
London behind a great Thames barrier, 2150
The Rhine-Ruhr grown into one hydrogen metropole, 2150

rules.description: Embargo: no travel to New Kingdom Egypt today.
Quarantine: no travel to Northern Song Kaifeng today.
Sakoku seal: no travel to Tokugawa Edo today.
Cholera quarantine: no travel to Victorian Britain today.
Border closed: no travel to Weimar Berlin today.
Typhoon warning: no travel to Showa Tokyo today.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: News? Only a rumour: someone sells pocket calculators to the ancients.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: They say a courier from your own century carries them. Watch for anyone who counts too fast.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Calculators? I saw nothing. Nothing at all.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: My temple at Deir el-Bahari rises in three terraces. The Pharaoh will be pleased.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Then my name will be chiselled off every wall. Let us hope your stamp is kind.

premades.name: Senenmut
premades.recordNote: Steward of the Pharaoh's household and architect of her temple.

premades.name: Socrates
premades.intro: Priority arrival: Socrates of Athens. He asks more questions than you do.
premades.recordNote: Philosopher. Known to question officials at length.

premades.name: Aspasia
premades.recordNote: Teacher of rhetoric. Keeps the company of Athens' first citizen.

premades.name: Ban Zhao
premades.recordNote: Court historian and tutor to the empress. Finishing her brother's history.

premades.name: Arib al-Ma'muniyya
premades.recordNote: Singer and poet of the caliph's court. Travels with her own musicians.

premades.name: Muhammad al-Khwarizmi
premades.recordNote: Scholar of the House of Wisdom. Writes on calculation.

premades.name: Johannes Gutenberg
premades.recordNote: Goldsmith of Mainz. Business in Strasbourg undisclosed.

premades.name: Leonardo da Vinci
premades.recordNote: Painter and engineer in the service of the Duke of Milan.

premades.name: Aemilia Lanyer
premades.recordNote: Poet of London, raised in a countess's household.

premades.name: Cecilia Gallerani
premades.recordNote: Lady of the Milanese court. Sat for a portrait with an ermine.

lines.leaderGained: HISTORY: {nation} now dominates the timeline. The Future belongs to {place}.
lines.leaderLost: HISTORY: {nation} no longer dominates the timeline. The Future is unsettled until a new power rises.

rules.name: Movable type reaches Florence
rules.news: HISTORY: Florentine printers set type the Chinese way, years before Gutenberg.

rules.name: The yen backs the Reichsmark
rules.news: HISTORY: Weimar Berlin's banks peg the Reichsmark to the yen.

rules.name: Al-jabr reaches Rome
rules.news: HISTORY: Roman engineers reckon with al-jabr tables from Baghdad.

rules.name: Sterling on the Nile
rules.news: HISTORY: Khedivate Cairo now trades in British sterling.

rules.name: Greek scribes in Thebes
rules.news: HISTORY: New Kingdom scribes now write in Greek.

rules.name: The mark crosses the Channel
rules.news: HISTORY: Post-war Britain pays in Deutsche Marks.

rules.name: Florins in the Morea
rules.news: HISTORY: Mystras now trades in Florentine florins.

rules.name: Hieroglyphs in Babylon
rules.news: HISTORY: Babylon's scribes carve hieroglyphs beside their cuneiform.

rules.name: The analytical engine runs
rules.news: HISTORY: Babbage's analytical engine hums in Victorian London.

rules.name: Steam in Athens
rules.news: HISTORY: Athenian engineers put the steam engine to work.

rules.name: An elected pharaoh
rules.news: HISTORY: Thebes votes: Hatshepsut now rules as an elected pharaoh.
